tasks.short: Develop visual concepts and sample layouts for commercial briefs.

steps.what: Read the brief, brand guidance, approved copy and channel requirements.

loop.input: Design brief, brand guidelines, approved copy and channel specifications.
loop.output: Design constraints with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields; designer checks source passages and conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved conflicts return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text briefs express priorities and restrictions inconsistently.

steps.what: Sketch alternative compositions in graphics software in the {OTHER}.

loop.input: Design constraints, approved assets and editable layout components.
loop.output: A small set of editable concept layouts.
loop.check: Check dimensions, required copy and asset use; designer judges hierarchy and originality.
loop.stop: Generate three candidates and allow one revision round; designer sketches missing directions manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle established formats, but this step explores new visual compositions.

steps.what: Compare concepts and choose a direction against the brief.
Refine typography, spacing and composition in graphics software in the {OTHER}.
Review the proof and approve the visual direction.
File the approved layout and update the project status.

tasks.design: A structured brief in the {PROJECT} links to approved assets and guidance in the {DOCS}; a bounded loop extracts constraints and drafts editable concepts in graphics software in the {OTHER}. The designer selects and refines the direction, while the {WORKFLOW} routes proof approval and files the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs, assets and feedback were disconnected. Bespoke composition still required substantial manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Editable concept generation is available, and AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting briefs, assets and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive composition, typography and coherent brand expression need experienced judgement. Generated concepts can converge on familiar visual patterns.
tasks.human_edge: The designer turns ambiguous commercial aims into a visual idea and recognises when an attractive layout communicates the wrong message.

ambition.what: A concept comparison session showing three genuinely different visual directions before production.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time assembling first drafts and more time developing and explaining visual directions. Marketing retains final approval; any delegated concept-selection authority must be agreed.

reach.task: Translate campaign objectives into concept evaluation criteria.
reach.learn: Audience priorities, campaign economics and how creative decisions support the intended response.

evidence.claim: Figma Make produces editable prototypes from prompts and a team's design system; suitability for each graphic format needs testing.
Figma Buzz supports locked template areas and spreadsheet-driven variants for established formats.
The supplied research reports higher output and ratings alongside lower average novelty among text-to-image adopters.
The proposed workflow, time allocation and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The baseline is a mixed in-house marketing design team with reusable brand assets.
Creation mainly happens on screen; the meeting-heavy prior overstates meetings for this task.
Concept approval is separate from permission to publish or place a print order.
Build ranges assume one pilot team and include access review and any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Whether approved assets and brand components are complete and consistently versioned.
Whether the graphics software in the {OTHER} exposes editable formats or supported interfaces.
Who can approve visual direction and which decisions the designer may make independently.
Whether employee consultation is required for the proposed workflow.
research_questions: Can generated concepts remain editable without losing typography or component structure?
Does concept generation produce materially different directions on representative briefs?
Which established formats can use configured templates without a model loop?
new_work: Check extracted constraints against their sources.
Reject repetitive or off-brand concepts.
Maintain approved components, templates and source links.
Monitor revision effort and approval delays during rollout.
tasks.statement: Create designs, concepts, and sample layouts, based on knowledge of layout principles and esthetic design concepts.

tasks.short: Choose composition, image sizes and typography for a clear visual hierarchy.

steps.what: Read the brief, approved copy, brand guide and output specifications.
Try image proportions and text arrangements in the design editor.
Choose type styles, sizes and spacing in the design editor.
Inspect the proof at intended size and adjust hierarchy and readability.
Save layout settings and explain the chosen arrangement for production.

tasks.design: A searchable library in {DOCS} presents approved specifications and links to reusable styles in the design editor in {OTHER}. Configured grids and text styles accelerate exploration, while the designer chooses hierarchy and optical adjustments. A deterministic exporter records selected settings in {DOCS} for production.
tasks.previous_blocker: Brand rules were scattered across documents, while reusable settings and production notes required separate upkeep.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing style and template features provide the foundation. Small exporters and validation scripts are cheaper to build with coding assistance.
tasks.still_hard: Optical balance, reading rhythm and unfamiliar scripts resist fixed rules. A screen preview may conceal print problems.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides what the audience should notice first and where a deliberate exception improves communication.

ambition.what: Large-print layouts for readers with low vision

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time rebuilding settings and documenting measurements. They can propose audience-specific layout standards, with approval from the brand owner before adoption.

reach.task: Translate visual hierarchy into responsive page layouts.
reach.learn: Responsive typography, semantic structure and accessibility testing.

evidence.claim: Template tools support locked regions and repeat variants, which can accelerate established layout patterns.
Style reuse and deterministic setting exports can reduce setup while leaving typographic judgement with the designer.

assumptions: Approved fonts, styles and production specifications exist.
The design editor exposes settings through an export or supported interface.
Reusable styles account for some preparation savings within manual typography work.
Screen-based design is the main means; physical proofs are used when required.
Time estimates cover one format family and are not measured savings.
Access estimates assume no new sensitive staff-data processing; national consultation rules still apply.
unknowns: Which formats, scripts and languages must be supported?
Are font licences valid for the intended outputs?
Which audience accessibility needs are currently underserved?
Who approves changes to the shared brand styles?
research_questions: Which layout settings can be exported without losing local overrides?
Which readability checks match the actual viewing and printing conditions?
new_work: Maintain shared styles and specification links.
Review exported settings for missing overrides.
Test unfamiliar languages and accessibility adaptations.
Retire templates that no longer match production requirements.
tasks.statement: Determine size and arrangement of illustrative material and copy, and select style and size of type.

tasks.short: Create and finish new digital images for marketing use.

steps.what: Define the subject, composition and intended use from the design brief.
Find approved reference images and check their permitted uses.
Construct candidate images in image-editing software in the {OTHER}.

loop.input: Image specification and references cleared for the intended processing and use.
loop.output: Candidate images with generation history and available provenance metadata.
loop.check: Check dimensions and metadata; designer inspects visual defects, factual fidelity and brief fit.
loop.stop: Two batches of four candidates maximum; switch to manual construction if neither batch works.
loop.why_not_simpler: New subjects and compositions cannot be produced through resizing or fixed templates alone.

steps.what: Select and retouch a candidate in image-editing software in the {OTHER}.
Approve the image for its stated marketing use.
Export delivery files and archive the approved master.

tasks.design: Approved references and usage records in the {DOCS} feed a bounded image-generation loop in image-editing software in the {OTHER}. The designer selects and retouches candidates; deterministic exports create channel files and preserve available provenance, with approval recorded through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creating each image required substantial manual construction. References, rights records and output versions were often stored separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Image generation and editing are established capabilities. Export scripts and structured asset records can connect them without autonomous agents.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate products, faces, text and consistent subjects across images remain demanding. Provenance metadata does not establish copyright ownership or clear third-party rights.
tasks.human_edge: The designer recognises misleading imagery, selects a compelling composition and finishes details that determine credibility.

ambition.what: A bounded custom-image service for internal event planners whose briefs previously received stock imagery.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time constructing initial images and more time directing, selecting and finishing them. Approval and publication rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Develop event imagery across invitations, signage and presentation screens.
reach.learn: Viewing distances, venue constraints, event milestones and attendee accessibility needs.

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio generates and edits images and attaches Content Credentials describing generation provenance.
A reported court decision denied copyright protection to three generated logos; it does not settle rights for every image workflow.
EU AI Act transparency duties distinguish machine-readable marking from disclosure obligations for particular uses.
The bounded generation budget and remaining-time estimates require validation on representative image briefs.

assumptions: This task concerns marketing imagery, with logos and legally sensitive depictions escalated for specialist review.
Most creation time is spent in software; the meeting-heavy prior does not fit this task.
Reference retrieval uses existing metadata and licence fields, without face recognition.
Access estimates include review of processing terms, personal data and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which reference assets may be submitted to an image-generation service.
Whether customer contracts require exclusive rights or prohibit generated imagery.
Whether provenance survives the actual export and publishing chain.
Which images depict identifiable people or confidential products.
research_questions: Which brief categories consistently yield usable candidates within the fixed generation budget?
Can export automation preserve required machine-readable marking and archive provenance?
Which image categories need manual production because factual fidelity dominates?
new_work: Inspect generated candidates for defects and misleading details.
Maintain reference permissions and generation records.
Check applicable disclosure requirements for the intended use.
Maintain export profiles and test provenance preservation.
tasks.statement: Use computer software to generate new images.

tasks.short: Assemble final print layouts, resolve production defects, and release approved files to the printer.

steps.what: Locate approved copy, artwork and printer specifications.
Place approved content into the layout template using the page-layout editor {OTHER}.
Adjust typography, image placement and page balance in the page-layout editor {OTHER}.
Add production marks and export the print package using the page-layout editor {OTHER}.
Check the print package and correct defects using the preflight tool {OTHER}.
Inspect the final visual proof and record requested corrections.
Approve the exact file version and send the print package.

tasks.design: Configure template population and export presets in the page-layout editor {OTHER}, with approved inputs held in the {DOCS}. A configured preflight tool {OTHER} applies printer-specific checks, while the {WORKFLOW} releases only the exact approved file version through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printer settings and approvals were scattered across files and mail. Reliable automation required consistent templates and a maintained production profile.
tasks.enabler_now: Template population, export presets and rule-based preflight already exist. AI coding makes the version checks and approval connection cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke layouts, complex folds, spot colours and unusual finishing need production expertise. A technically valid file can still look wrong.
tasks.human_edge: The designer judges typography and visual balance, and recognises when production constraints damage the intended design.

ambition.what: Let event planners request approved-format print materials through a controlled intake form.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time placing routine content and packaging files, with more time for layout quality and production exceptions. Print-release authority stays with the existing approver.

reach.task: Resolve print-production defects before supplier handoff.
reach.learn: Preflight profiles, overprint, bleed, colour separation and packaging conventions.

reach.task: Specify event signage and printed collateral.
reach.learn: Viewing distance, physical dimensions, finishing requirements and supplier deadlines.

evidence.claim: Enfocus PitStop Pro checks PDF/X profiles, applies action lists and reports production issues.
Figma Buzz supports locked template areas and spreadsheet-fed variants, demonstrating controlled content substitution.
Template assembly and technical preflight can be automated while final visual judgement remains human.
Build ranges and remaining effort are estimates for a small set of recurring print formats.

assumptions: Digital page-layout assembly is typical; physical paste-up is exceptional.
Recurring formats have approved templates; bespoke refinement remains a separate human step.
Preflight automatically fixes only explicitly permitted, tested defects and preserves the original.
A changed file invalidates its previous release approval.
Routine file preparation uses system screens more than the meeting-heavy prior suggests.
unknowns: Which recurring formats have stable templates.
Whether printers supply machine-readable specifications or maintained profiles.
Which preflight corrections the team permits automatically.
Whether the designer may release files or another role must approve.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Which production defects can safely be corrected without changing visual intent?
How consistently do supplier profiles detect finishing-specific failures?
new_work: Maintain printer profiles and approved templates.
Review unresolved preflight exceptions.
Verify that approval refers to the exact released file.
Test representative physical proofs when profiles or suppliers change.
Handle rejected deliveries and supplier specification changes.
tasks.statement: Mark up, paste, and assemble final layouts to prepare layouts for printer.

tasks.short: Create computer artwork and charts, review them, and produce printed proofs.

steps.what: Gather approved content, data and specifications for the artwork.
Draw charts from supplied data using the design editor {OTHER}.
Draw illustrations and other artwork using the design editor {OTHER}.

loop.input: Approved visual brief, permitted reference assets and output constraints.
loop.output: Up to three illustration candidates with generation metadata.
loop.check: Check dimensions and file integrity; designer checks meaning, visual defects, rights and suitability.
loop.stop: One generation batch and one correction batch; unsuitable results return to manual drawing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Original illustrative content cannot be obtained by chart rules or template substitution alone.

steps.what: Refine composition, chart readability and illustration details in the design editor {OTHER}.
Export a proof and check technical settings in the design editor {OTHER}.
Check the proof and print through the print driver {OTHER}.

tasks.design: A portable artwork generator takes approved files from the {DOCS}, renders charts deterministically and uses a bounded image-generation loop in the creative tool {OTHER} for suitable illustration drafts. The designer refines the master; configured export checks preserve available provenance and require approval before printing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts were redrawn by hand and creative files lacked consistent input contracts. Illustration generation also offered limited control over detail and repeatability.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding lowers the cost of chart renderers, asset importers and validation. Existing image generation can supply draft candidates, while export presets handle routine production.
tasks.still_hard: Precise technical illustrations, consistent characters and editable vector structure remain difficult. Generated drafts can require more correction than manual drawing.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides what the image should communicate and catches misleading visual emphasis, poor composition and subtle drawing errors.

ambition.what: A recurring branded chart pack generated from approved campaign data.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time plotting data and preparing proofs, and more time on visual explanation. They can propose chart treatments earlier; publication and production spending retain existing approval rights.

reach.task: Turn campaign findings into accurate explanatory charts.
reach.learn: Denominators, uncertainty, axis choices and the limits of the source data.

reach.task: Prepare reliable artwork exports for publication.
reach.learn: Colour profiles, font handling and output specifications.

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio generates and edits images and attaches Content Credentials.
Enfocus PitStop Pro checks PDF production requirements and reports issues.
Deterministic chart generation can preserve numeric correspondence with supplied data.
The cited adoption study reports increased output alongside reduced average novelty; it does not establish savings here.

assumptions: The time split represents a mixed workload of charts and illustrative artwork; individual jobs may contain only one.
Charts use approved structured data; illustrations are promotional rather than safety-critical technical instructions.
Computer creation dominates this task, so the prior's large meeting share is reduced.
Available provenance metadata is retained through tested export paths.
Build ranges are estimates for one reusable chart family and one illustration workflow.
unknowns: The actual balance of charts, original illustrations and reusable artwork.
Whether current creative tools expose usable scripting and export interfaces.
Which assets may be sent to an image-generation service.
Whether personal images or employee data trigger additional GDPR review or national consultation requirements.
Who approves printing and any associated spending.
research_questions: Which export paths preserve provenance metadata across required artwork formats?
Which illustration categories consistently require less correction than drawing from scratch?
new_work: Maintain chart templates and validate data mappings.
Review generated artwork and record rejected candidates.
Check permitted asset use and applicable disclosure requirements.
Test export presets after creative-tool updates.
Monitor generation costs and manual fallback frequency.
tasks.statement: Draw and print charts, graphs, illustrations, and other artwork, using computer.

tasks.short: Review final layouts and recommend improvements before approval.

steps.what: Locate the current proof, brief and previous review comments.
Check technical specifications using the design editor and PDF preflight tool.
Assess hierarchy, readability, brand fit and message in the proof document.
Discuss recommendations and resolve conflicting feedback with the marketing manager.
Record approval or return the proof for revision.

tasks.design: A configured {WORKFLOW} assembles the current proof and comments from {DOCS}, then invokes technical checks in the preflight tool in {OTHER}. Designers review the exceptions and make visual recommendations. The marketing manager records a version-specific decision in {WORKFLOW}, which routes revisions or marks the proof approved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical checks were separate from proof discussions, and approvals often referred to ambiguous attachments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing preflight profiles and configurable review flows cover much of the coordination without model judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A technically valid layout can still communicate badly. Stakeholders may disagree about audience, tone or acceptable compromise.
tasks.human_edge: The designer explains why a change helps the audience and negotiates a coherent result.
tasks.altitude: Review time shifts toward visual reasoning and stakeholder decisions. The designer can recommend release readiness with clearer evidence; publication approval remains with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Check whether layout changes alter meaning or hide essential copy.
reach.learn: Proof marks, reading order and editorial escalation.

evidence.claim: PDF preflight software checks PDF/X profiles and reports issues; action lists can perform specified fixes.
Visual judgement and feedback negotiation remain human work; technical checks support only part of the review.

assumptions: Print proofs are included; digital formats need different checks.
Technical checks report issues without silently changing approved artwork.
The marketing manager is the publication approver in this typical workflow.
Time shares include the approval handoff and are planning estimates.
Consultation estimates assume approval records are not repurposed for employee monitoring; national rules vary.
unknowns: Which production profiles and digital accessibility requirements apply?
Who can approve which channels and spending levels?
Are proof annotations exportable and tied to immutable versions?
What access and consultation are required for approval records?
research_questions: Which checks produce actionable findings rather than excessive warnings?
How reliably does the review flow prevent approval of an obsolete version?
new_work: Maintain channel-specific check profiles.
Triage technical warnings and document accepted exceptions.
Maintain reviewer roles and approval routing.
Check that revisions invalidate earlier approvals.
tasks.statement: Review final layouts and suggest improvements, as needed.

tasks.short: Discuss layout needs with clients and agree a workable design direction.

steps.what: Review the brief, earlier feedback and layout options before the discussion.

loop.input: Current brief, layout proof notes and the relevant feedback thread.
loop.output: A source-linked agenda of open questions, constraints and contradictory requests.
loop.check: Designer checks each issue against the source and removes unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous points remain questions for the meeting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client intent and conflicting preferences are expressed in free text.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and share the current proof.
Explain audience needs, preferences and practical constraints.
Explain layout trade-offs, challenge conflicts and explore alternatives with the client.
Agree the direction, requested changes and unresolved decisions.
Write a recap of decisions, changes, responsibilities and open questions.

loop.input: Designer-entered meeting notes, explicit decisions and agreed changes.
loop.output: A recap separating agreed actions from unresolved questions.
loop.check: Designer verifies commitments, owners and dates against the notes.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing details stay blank or become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes require interpretation to become a clear client-facing recap.

steps.what: Check and send the recap to the client.
Record agreed changes and update the project tasks.

tasks.design: A bounded preparation loop reads the current brief and relevant feedback from the {DOCS}, {PROJECT} and {EMAIL}, while the {CALENDAR} handles routine scheduling. The conversation and agreement stay human; a second bounded loop drafts the recap from designer notes, and the {WORKFLOW} sends the approved recap and records structured actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions were embedded in conversations and email threads. Scheduling, recaps and project updates were handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction and drafting can work from selected source material. Existing scheduling and workflow configuration can handle the surrounding administration.
tasks.still_hard: Clients may disagree internally or express preferences indirectly. A summary cannot establish agreement that was never reached.
tasks.human_edge: The designer builds trust, notices hesitation and helps clients choose between competing aims without promising an unworkable solution.

ambition.what: A pre-design alignment workshop for internal teams commissioning their first campaign.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time preparing and documenting discussions and more time resolving ambiguity with clients. Commercial commitments and client approval rights remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Align stakeholders on campaign priorities before creative production.
reach.learn: Stakeholder facilitation, scope negotiation and the campaign approval process.

evidence.claim: Client advice, feasibility discussion and final selection remain human; preparation and documentation can be handled separately.
Source-linked extraction and bounded recap drafting are feasible patterns, but the digest supplies no measured case for this meeting workflow.
GDPR applies when client correspondence or meeting notes contain personal data.

assumptions: Client includes internal commissioning teams as well as external clients.
Scheduling uses a designer-selected participant list and approved availability windows.
The workflow uses designer notes and does not require meeting recording.
Each recap stores structured actions so approved fields can populate project tasks without another model call.
Build ranges include access, retention review and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which client communications the preparation workflow may access.
Who may commit to scope, cost and delivery dates.
Whether informal meeting agreement is sufficient or written client approval is required.
Which retention and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration remove the routine coordination step?
Does the recap reliably distinguish a suggestion from an agreed commitment?
Which preparation fields improve the discussion enough to justify their review time?
new_work: Check agenda sources and remove irrelevant client history.
Verify recap commitments before sending.
Resolve disputed or incomplete decisions with the client.
Maintain access scopes, retention settings and action templates.
tasks.statement: Confer with clients to discuss and determine layout design.

tasks.short: Create graphics and layouts for product illustrations, logos and websites.

steps.what: Clarify audience, message and creative constraints with the marketing manager.
Explore visual concepts and rough compositions in the design editor.

loop.input: Creative direction, permitted reference assets, brand constraints and requested output dimensions.
loop.output: Up to three rough visual concepts with available generation provenance.
loop.check: Validate files and dimensions mechanically; the designer checks relevance, visual defects, product accuracy and suitability.
loop.stop: Generate three candidates and allow one revision batch; then stop and fall back to manual exploration.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover established formats but cannot supply unfamiliar visual interpretations of an open creative brief.

steps.what: Select and refine artwork in the design editor, checking accuracy and asset rights.
Review the artwork with the marketing manager and agree acceptance or changes.
Export accepted artwork from the design editor and store production files.

tasks.design: A bounded generator in {OTHER} produces rough concepts from a brief in {DOCS}; the designer selects, redraws and refines the result. A configured {WORKFLOW} records acceptance of a specific artwork version before export presets in {OTHER} create production assets in {DOCS}. Available provenance and rights records travel with the assets.
tasks.previous_blocker: Early visual exploration took substantial drawing time, while automated exports did little to help interpret an open brief.
tasks.enabler_now: Image generation offers quick rough candidates, and existing export presets handle repeat production work. Small integrations can now be built more cheaply, without delegating creative acceptance.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive logos, accurate product details, editable geometry and coherent brand systems still take skilled work. Generated output does not establish ownership or clearance.
tasks.human_edge: The designer creates a defensible visual idea, judges cultural meaning and turns rough material into a coherent identity.

ambition.what: Early visual concept testing with customer panels

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from making every rough option by hand toward developing and testing selected ideas. The designer can recommend which concepts deserve customer testing; brand acceptance and publication rights remain assigned separately.

reach.task: Test whether visual concepts communicate the intended message.
reach.learn: Neutral test prompts, audience sampling and separating preference from comprehension.

reach.task: Prepare graphics for responsive website use.
reach.learn: Asset formats, responsive crops, performance budgets and accessible alternatives.

evidence.claim: Image generation and editing tools can attach machine-readable Content Credentials describing generation provenance.

Rough-concept generation needs human selection, and task-specific savings require a local pilot.

tasks.short: Enter approved copy and artwork into layouts for review.

steps.what: Find the current brief, approved copy, artwork and layout plan.
Prepare copy and image files for placement in the design editor.
Place copy and artwork into frames in the design editor.
Correct overflow, awkward crops and spacing in the design editor.
Send the layout proof and version details for review.

tasks.statement: Key information into computer equipment to create layouts for client or supervisor.

tasks.short: Develop visual sketches, discuss them with stakeholders and revise the chosen direction.

steps.what: Read the campaign brief and reference assets in the {DOCS}.
Draw rough visual routes on paper or in the {OTHER} illustration editor.

loop.input: Designer-written visual directions, approved references and brand constraints.
loop.output: Up to three rough visual routes for internal exploration.
loop.check: Designer checks relevance, visual defects, inappropriate content and reference permissions; retain provenance metadata.
loop.stop: Three routes and one revision round per route; return to manual sketching if unsuitable.

Assemble and send concept proofs through the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.
Discuss concept proofs and agree changes with the marketing manager.

Approve the revised artwork and record the decision through the {EMAIL}.

reach.learn: Positioning, audience response and how concept choices affect campaign objectives.

reach.task: Develop an event identity before commissioning final collateral.
